title: Runtime: bounded request queue + early shed at scheduler boundary
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: Under burst traffic we currently allow the runtime ingress queue to grow unbounded (or effectively unbounded via per-worker pending lists). When GPU pools saturate, this leads to (1) queue blowups, (2) tail-latency collapse, (3) increased cancellation/timeout churn, and (4) memory pressure amplification as prefills accumulate. This PR introduces a bounded queue at the scheduler boundary and deterministic early shedding before a request is admitted into prefill/decode scheduling.

What’s in this PR: 1) Bounded scheduler ingress queue: Add a capacity-limited queue in the runtime scheduler. Requests are admitted only if there is room in the bounded queue; otherwise we shed immediately with an explicit overload reason returned to the control plane. Capacity is configurable per model profile (default based on max_concurrent_prefills + decode_slots) and can be overridden at runtime via config hot reload.

2) Deterministic shed point (pre-scheduling): Shedding happens at the scheduler boundary (before prefill is enqueued). This avoids partially-started requests and prevents mid-stream disconnects caused by internal queue churn. Streaming requests are never shed once tokens have begun emitting; we only shed prior to scheduling.

3) Backpressure plumbing: The runtime returns a structured error to the routing/control plane: category=overload, reason=RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL, retryable=true, retry_after_ms=<hint>. Note: HTTP mapping is handled at gateway/routing layers; this PR only standardizes the runtime-side signal and metadata.

4) Telemetry: Add counters/gauges/histograms for queue depth, shed count, shed reason, and admission latency at the scheduler boundary. Metrics are low-cardinality (labels: model_family, region, pool_id, reason) per the ongoing overload-protection observability guidance.

5) Unit tests + perf characterization: Adds scheduler tests for admission/concurrency edge cases, fairness under mixed request sizes, and streaming invariants. Perf characterization includes synthetic overload runs showing stable p99 under overload and reduced time-to-recovery after spikes.

Feature flagging / rollout: This is gated behind runtime.overload_protection.bounded_queue.enabled (default off). When enabled, we set conservative defaults (queue_capacity_factor=1.5, retry_after_ms=250) and rely on routing-level breakers for coarse throttling.

Perf notes (single A100 80GB / fp16, 7B/13B class models, internal perf harness): Baseline under 2.5x overload: p99 end-to-end latency degrades until clients time out (queue grows). With bounded queue: p99 stabilizes (bounded waiting) and we shed ~18–25% at peak with clear retryable errors; throughput remains within ±2% of baseline at saturation. Recovery time after spike (time to return to steady p95) improved from ~6–8 min to ~45–70s due to avoiding deep backlog.

Risk/mitigations: Main risk is being too aggressive and shedding while there is usable capacity (false positives). We mitigate with capacity derived from scheduler slots and a small headroom factor, plus metrics to tune per model family. We also ensure no shedding after streaming starts to preserve client correctness.

Follow-ups (out of scope here): End-to-end overload reason code mapping in gateway + OpenAI-compat error shape (tracked separately), plus integrating memory-pressure guardrails (separate PR) and game-day validation.

snippet: Illustrative snippet (scheduler admission): if (!boundedQueue.tryEnqueue(req)) { return OverloadError.runtimeQueueFull({ retryAfterMs: cfg.retryAfterMs, queueDepth: boundedQueue.depth(), capacity: boundedQueue.capacity() }); }
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The approach makes sense, but I’m worried about shedding after a request is already partially registered. Can we guarantee the shed point is strictly before prefill scheduling and before any stream headers are emitted?

Marcus Reed (author): Yep — shed is before enqueueing into prefill work. I added a streaming invariant test: once first_token_emitted=true we bypass queue admission logic entirely. Also updated comments in scheduler.ts to make the invariant explicit.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Metric labels: please avoid request_route or model_id raw values. Use model_family and pool_id only (pool_id bounded).
Marcus Reed (author): Agreed. Removed route label and replaced model_id with model_family (derived from model profile). pool_id is stable and bounded. Updated metrics docstring and tests.
Christine Wong (review): Please add a retry hint that routing can translate to Retry-After. Also can we surface a single, stable reason code string for dashboards/runbooks?

Marcus Reed (author): Added retry_after_ms to the runtime overload metadata and set reason=RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL. Note routing/gateway will do HTTP mapping in other PRs; here we just ensure the signal exists end-to-end in the runtime/control-plane RPC.

Noah Patel (review): Lock contention: boundedQueue.tryEnqueue() uses a mutex; under overload this could be hot. Can we use a lock-free counter for capacity and keep the queue append protected only when admitting?

Marcus Reed (author): Updated implementation: fast-path uses an atomic inFlight counter and only takes the queue lock on successful admission. Under overload, we fail fast without lock acquisition. Added a microbench in tests to validate contention behavior.
Sofia Ivanova (review): Approved after the streaming invariant and lock contention changes.
Noah Patel (review): Approved. Please add a short note in the perf README about how to reproduce the overload run and which knobs to tweak.
perf_results: Repro steps in tools/perf/overload/README.md. Summary: At 2.5x target RPS for 10 minutes, bounded queue keeps scheduler queue depth <= capacity (flat), shed rate peaks at ~22% and drops to <1% within ~60s after load normalizes. p99 latency during overload is bounded by queue wait + prefill/decode scheduling (~3.2s p99 vs unbounded >30s leading to client timeouts). Throughput at saturation is unchanged within noise; CPU overhead of admission check measured at ~0.3–0.6% in the runtime process under overload due to lock-free fast-path.
testing_notes: Unit tests: scheduler admission/eviction invariants, streaming no-shed-after-first-token, retry_after_ms propagation to control-plane client, metrics emission. Manual: ran canary runtime in staging with overload harness; validated shed errors show up as overload category in routing logs and that active streams are not interrupted.
release_notes: Runtime overload protection: optional bounded scheduler queue + deterministic early shedding under overload (feature-flagged). Adds runtime telemetry for queue depth and shed reasons.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; feature flag remains OFF by default pending routing/gateway integration and canary rollout plan.
